comparator.name: Musicology (Muziekwetenschap)
comparator.academicYear: 2026–27 UvA programme for a Fall 2026 entrant, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official common curriculum and 2026–27 study guide reconcile to an exact 60+60+60=180 EC full-time pathway. The normalized target names no specialization, so the first-listed Cognitive and Computational Musicology route is selected under the neutral official-order rule. Year 1 is a 60-EC foundation in musicology, Western music history, cultural musicology, cognition, music theory, solfège, harmony, repertoire and Music and AI. The selected year-2 programme consists of 48 EC of common methods, analysis, philosophy and research work plus 12 EC of route courses. Year 3 combines a 6-EC route course with the published 6-EC programme-bound choice, 36 EC open choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. The public schedule displays common choice slots while the study guide supplies route content; alternatives are not added together. The same curriculum can be taken part-time over six years, but this reconstruction uses the standard full-time structure.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names no specialization. The official 2026–27 study guide lists Cognitive and Computational Musicology first, before Cultural Musicology and Historical Musicology, so that route is selected independently of UCR fit. Repertoire emphases such as jazz, popular, classical and world music remain alternatives rather than additive requirements.

exception.reason: The defining curriculum begins with compulsory general music theory, two successive solfège and harmony/analysis courses, score reading and analysis, four chronological Western music-history courses, cultural musicology, music cognition and academic study of musical cultures. It then requires music ethnography, popular-music studies, quantitative musicology, philosophy and research projects, specialization work in computational and cognitive musicology and rhythm, and an independent musicology thesis. The current UCR catalogue has no course in music theory, solfège, harmony, score analysis, music history, ethnomusicology or musicology research methods, and no sustained music-cognition sequence. A 24-course programme assembled from general film, media, literature, art history, cognition, sociology and computing would replace the target’s central object of study and disciplinary progression rather than provide a defensible closest match. Even the 42 EC of genuinely open choice cannot compensate for the absent compulsory musicological core.
exception.curriculumContext: The selected full-time route totals exactly 180 EC: a 60-EC first year, a 48-EC common second-year programme plus 12 EC of Cognitive and Computational Musicology, and a third year with 6 EC of route study, 6 EC programme-bound choice, 36 EC genuine free choice and a 12-EC musicology thesis. The public curriculum presents the common schedule and the study guide provides specialization detail; choices and specializations are not treated as cumulative. The exception rests on the missing UCR discipline and progression, not on credit ambiguity or on performance training.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current enriched UCR course workbook, including course names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, prerequisites, planned terms and topics. GOSHIST311 Native American Histories includes Indigenous music within one historical topic; MCCCOMM312 Creative Communication Laboratory may use sonic poetry while explicitly not constituting music performance or songwriting; MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCMEDI111 Introduction to Film & Media can address sound as part of audiovisual form; MCCHEAM111 Introduction to Western Art History supplies broad cultural history; HCBCOGN311 Higher Order Functions and HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics provide adjacent cognitive study; and DISARIN311 Optimization Methods in AI supplies computational methods. These are isolated encounters or neighbouring disciplines. None teaches notation, ear training, harmony, score analysis, historical repertoires, ethnomusicological fieldwork, systematic music cognition or musicology research as a coherent sequence. The workbook therefore provides no defensible basis for a scheduled 24-course UCR Musicology programme.
